scope: Independent correctness and source/complexity review of complete split-divisor translation; no independent performance measurements.

independence.expected_group_law: Construct line/cubic intersection polynomial, divide out known input abscissas including tangent multiplicity, negate third intersection. This does not call production point_add or rational translation maps.
independence.expected_divisors: Python integer polynomial product and Lagrange interpolation; enumerate F_p to decode every output polynomial in complete-translation checks.
independence.internal_identities: Direct scalar sums over known roots, independent products of distinct image factors, and direct partial-fraction numerator sums. No production polynomial arithmetic is used to form expected values.

mutations.reason: translated point multiset differs from geometry

independence.limitation: The geometric oracle shares the mathematical group law and curve model, but uses a different computational construction. This is extensive testing and source review, not a formal verification.

mathematical_review.image_multiplicity: Translation is a bijection on E(F_p). A finite x coordinate has at most two points, so a simple input's translated x fibers have size one or two. A size-two fiber consists of opposite points and cannot be a 2-torsion point.
mathematical_review.trace_minimal_polynomial: Unweighted projected moments are sum_j m_j lambda_j^k with distinct lambda_j and m_j in {1,2}. Since p>3, each m_j is nonzero. The corresponding Vandermonde/diagonal-weight Hankel form has full rank equal to the number of distinct images. Therefore 2d moments determine their squarefree image polynomial, including zero images and d>=p.
mathematical_review.multiplicity_and_ordinate_recovery: For q(T)=product_j(T-lambda_j), N_a(lambda_j)=m_j q'(lambda_j). Thus N_a/q' separates multiplicities by gcd with 1 and 2. The weighted numerator N_b/q' equals the sum of ordinates in a fiber; on singleton fibers this is its unique ordinate. On double fibers both signs are recovered separately by split-algebra square root.
mathematical_review.small_characteristic: The logarithmic-derivative trace series uses no division by moment index. No d
mathematical_review.exceptions: The x=x_Q support factor is removed before denominator inversion. It maps to 2Q or infinity by the affine group law. Input infinity maps to Q. Q=infinity returns the original divisor. All are included in complete timing.
mathematical_review.paper_preconditions: Paper Algorithm 3 assumes p>3, a nonsquare beta, split simple components, and excludes both Q and -Q from their support. The implementation extends exceptional support handling and supplies a charged nonsquare search when beta is not provided.

complexity_review.trace_projection: For m=ceil(sqrt(2d)) and q=ceil(2d/m), constructs an A matrix of shape (2q,d), a B matrix of shape (d,m), and computes A*B. Baby/giant powers and Hankel-to-convolution dual conversion require about sqrt(d) degree-d polynomial operations. Matrix/baby storage is O(d^(3/2)) field entries, with additional Python/native copies.
complexity_review.matrix_cost: Classical rectangular multiplication costs O(d^2) field operations. Blocking with fast square multiplication gives the familiar O(d^((omega+1)/2)) upper bound. This source review does not establish which multiplication algorithm FLINT selects at measured dimensions.
complexity_review.remaining_quadratic_work: The supplied native Berlekamp-Massey implementation is quadratic in sequence length and performs modular inversion by exponentiation at nonzero discrepancies. Its field-operation bound is O(d^2+d log p). Thus this implementation does not attain a subquadratic complete-translation bound or confirm the paper's proposed exponent as implemented.
complexity_review.dense_route: Forms a full d by d multiplication matrix and computes its characteristic polynomial; inverse composition forms and solves a dense singleton-degree square system. The paper's theoretical dense bound is O(d^omega) plus polynomial algebra and lifting. Actual native backend algorithms and constants need measured comparison.
complexity_review.collision_lift: Shared by both routes. For p=3 mod 4 it uses modular exponentiation. Otherwise it uses Sylow splitting by GCD/modular powers and pairwise CRT. There is no factor() or roots() call in the timed translation source. For supplied beta, a standard soft-O(M(d) log^2 p) allowance covers the split-algebra square-root route; this is not a new root-finding algorithm.
complexity_review.nonsquare_search: Default general-p calls deterministically try beta=2,3,... and charge that search inside translation. No unconditional polynomial-in-log(p) deterministic bound for this search is asserted. Supplying a validated beta changes that precomputation assumption and must be reported.
complexity_review.novelty: Paper section 8.1 explicitly proposes trace power projections and inverse modular composition. This implementation is an audited realization with a quadratic recurrence step, not a claim to invent the trace idea.

benchmark_review.timed_boundary: benchmark.py times the complete translate call including field/poly conversion, checks, rational map, reconstruction, collision lifting, nonsquare search when required, and exceptional handling. Both methods receive the same (u,v) input. Input construction and C++ helper build/loading precede timing and are disclosed.
benchmark_review.comparison_scope: The dense method reproduces the paper's dense-matrix reconstruction route using the same native polynomial/matrix backend. It shares the new implementation's collision lifting and exception handling with trace. This is not a literal runtime reproduction of the paper's original Magma program or an optimal-algorithm comparison.
benchmark_review.process_cost: Fresh-child CPU/wall and peak RSS are retained separately from the algorithm call; fresh-child totals include process imports, validation and other harness overhead. Peak RSS includes interpreter and native libraries; it is not a measure of polynomial data alone.
benchmark_review.fixture_generation: Timing fixture creation uses known roots and production affine point_add outside both methods. Independent audit supplies separate correctness evidence. Excluded fixture construction is legitimate for translation input (u,v), but cannot be excluded from a complete labelled-pool relation-generation cost.
benchmark_review.machine_scope: CPU-pinned shared container, one FLINT thread; not a dedicated host. Measured speed ratios must be tied to exact fields, degrees, collision patterns, source hashes, and repetitions.

limitations: Production field API is a prime 3<p<2^63, short nonsingular Weierstrass model. It does not implement binary fields or direct 256-bit prime arithmetic.

Primality and splitting of u are trusted preconditions. Runtime checks reject nonmonic, nonsquarefree and off-curve inputs, but do not promise rejection of arbitrary nonsplit or composite-modulus inputs.
Supported input is a simple finite divisor with at most one point per x, plus at most one infinity. General repeated effective divisors require a separate representation and are outside this API.
Large-prime tests check internal identities for d<=13 without enumerating a large field. Complete end-to-end translations are checked only over the listed small fields.
The audit does not certify cryptographic constant-time behavior, malformed Python object handling, extension fields, threading, or every compiler/platform.

No improved incidence-GCD bound, relation-generation exponent, or complete ECDLP complexity follows from this translation check. Structured factor bases and mixed labelled pools remain separate constructions with separate costs.
